explanation: Sodium oxide dissolves in water to form sodium hydroxide — one of NCERT's two examples of a metal oxide soluble enough to form an alkali directly.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: White sodium oxide powder in water.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A clear, colourless sodium hydroxide solution.
beaker_view.observation: The white powder dissolves completely into the water, forming a clear solution.
